newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Winterthur expects China licence soon.
newsitem.headline: Winterthur expects China licence soon.

text.p: Winterthur Insurance Co confirmed China had agreed in principle to make it the first European insurer to get a licence there and said it expected to get definite approval for non-life business soon.

"The competent authorities have taken the decision in principle for Winterthur to take up business operations in the People's Republic of China," the company said, confirming remarks Switzerland's president made in Beijing on Friday.

"We may expect to receive the definitive licence for non-life operations in the Shanghai region in the near future," Winterthur added in a statement, saying it would make its business plan public once it had received final approval.

"This is good news. Things are on the right track but it is not quite definitive yet, which is why we are being rather cautious," company spokeswoman Anna-Marie Kappeler said. She said the licence could be issued as early as next month.
Kappeler gave no forecast for how big its China business might be, but made clear Winterthur saw great potential.
"This is an important market. We see great possibilities for the market or else we would not have put as much effort into this," she told Reuters.

Swiss President Jean-Pascal Delamuraz broke the news to reporters in the Chinese capital on Friday. The decision put Winterthur at the head of a queue of 80 foreign insurers awaiting licences for the fast-growing Chinese market.
Winterthur has four representative offices in China and has sought to build up expertise in the market, but has not been entitled to sell policies there.
China has been opening up its domestic insurance market slowly, fearing that foreign competitors might overwhelm the once heavily protected industry.

Beijing has already allowed American International Assurance Co Ltd and Tokio Marine and Fire Insurance Co Ltd to conduct business directly and a Hong Kong unit of Manufacturers Life Insurance Co of Canada has gained approval for a joint venture with the cash-rich state oil trader Sinochem.

American International Assurance, part of the American International Group, has been particularly successful. It has forced domestic competitors in the Shanghai market to adopt many of its practices, such as paying bigger commissions on insurance policy sales.
Winterthur's Australian subsidiary HIH Winterthur is also operating in the Chinese market via a joint venture.
Chinese insurance officials have said that they expected to see a trend toward joint ventures as the market opens up to foreign concerns.
